comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum applies to 2026-2027 and accounts for 180 EC. Year 1 has ten compulsory 6-EC components covering mathematics, two Principles of Economics and Business courses, accounting, microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics, a research project, markets and organisations, and finance. Year 2 has five named common 6-EC courses plus 30 EC of major specialisation. Year 3 preserves a genuine 30-EC free-choice semester and 30 EC of specialisation courses plus the thesis. The normalized target is the generic Economics and Business Economics bachelor. After the common first 18 months, students choose Economics or Business Economics; Business Economics then requires a further third-year specialisation in Accounting and Control, Finance or Organisational Economics, while Economics permits a suitable-course curriculum without another named specialisation. The Economics major is therefore selected under the neutral least-specialized-general rule, before and independently of UCR course selection. The official public curriculum does not disaggregate the two 30-EC major bundles into stable named course-and-credit components, so those bundles are preserved exactly rather than filled with invented options.
components: Officially preserved 30-EC major bundle; the public curriculum does not disaggregate it into stable named components.

alternatives.label: Economics, business and data
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible response to Economics and Business Economics combining markets, macroeconomics and policy with accounting, finance, strategy, organisations, statistics, data and econometrics.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, mathematical and strategic foundations precede the advanced policy, organisational, international-business, machine-learning, econometrics, behavioural-economics, market-research and finance work. Strategy follows Business Foundations; Probability & Statistics follows Mathematical Methods; Money, Banking & Finance follows business, accounting and economic study. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.
traceOverrides: provides multivariate statistics and experimental methods that strengthen empirical economic and business research

alternatives.label: Public economics, institutions and inequality
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum makes public economics, political institutions, law, inequality and policy research its organising emphasis while retaining economics and quantitative foundations.
alternatives.concept: A public-economics route combining economic theory and empirical analysis with government, institutions, inequality, law, governance and public policy.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces accounting, marketing, business strategy, international business, product design, machine learning, probability and finance with comparative politics, sociology, qualitative methods, political philosophy, human rights, constitutional law, sustainability governance, EU politics, social theory, persuasive communication, peace and conflict, and historical research. The resulting curriculum is organised around institutions and policy rather than firms and business functions.
progression: Foundational economics, politics and sociology precede advanced public economics, governance, constitutional law, EU politics, social theory, policy communication and research. Qualitative Research Methodology precedes the final research seminar; Research Methods & Statistics precedes econometrics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics and quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around finance and economics with substantial mathematics, programming, data, econometrics and optimisation, rather than implying a specialist finance degree without a quantitative core.
alternatives.concept: A financial-economics route combining money, banking and corporate finance with micro- and macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics, probability, calculus, programming, databases, machine learning and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It therefore retains the economics and business core while making quantitative financial and economic analysis the organising emphasis. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.
progression: Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and Money, Banking & Finance. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra and Advanced Calculus; programming precedes computational decision-making; accounting, economics, data and research foundations precede the final finance, econometrics and behavioural-economics work. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and all courses are offered in their assigned terms.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the generic Economics and Business Economics bachelor. After the common first 18 months, the official curriculum requires a choice between Economics and Business Economics. Business Economics then branches again into Accounting and Control, Finance or Organisational Economics, while Economics allows students to design a suitable-course curriculum without a further named specialisation. Economics is therefore the least specialised general route, selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme-wide economics, business and empirical core. Direct and stable programme interests support two further coherent directions: public economics with institutions and policy, and finance with quantitative analysis. Both produce feasible curricula that are substantively distinct from the closest match and from each other. Accounting, control and organisational economics remains supportable, but production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

blocks: Both establish economic and business-economic foundations and apply them to real-world choices.
Both analyse consumer and firm choice, market structure and strategic interaction.
Both examine aggregate economic performance, banking and macroeconomic policy.
Both examine firms, markets, organisational incentives and strategic decision-making.
Both introduce financial statements, accounting information and corporate-finance reasoning.
Both examine banking, financial decision-making and monetary or financial risk.

The comparator has a dedicated introductory finance course. UCR finance content is integrated across Accounting & Corporate Finance and Money, Banking & Finance, both already shown once at their full credit weight.
UCR includes international macroeconomics and international business, but no single scheduled course reproduces the comparator focus on international money and finance.
This is the official 30-EC Economics-major specialisation bundle; it is preserved without inventing a course-level UCR equivalence.
Both provide mathematical techniques for quantitative economic analysis.
Both develop research design, data analysis and the practical execution of an empirical project.
UCR data science develops data preparation, visualisation and empirical analysis that directly supports the comparator statistics component.
Both use regression and statistical models to answer economic questions with real-world data.
Both develop estimation, hypothesis testing and interpretation of quantitative evidence; UCR frames these through experimental methods.
Both develop academic study, research-question and literature-review skills, though the UCR course is broader personal and professional formation.
Both develop critical reflection on the grounds and implications of economic or public judgment; the comparator course is specifically economic methodology.
This is genuine free-choice space. UCR flexibility is distributed across the complete 180-EC curriculum, so no single course is asserted as its equivalent.

This official bundle combines Economics-major specialisation work and the bachelor thesis. UCR optional independent research is displayed alongside it as a comparison-only element without inventing a component split.

notes.text: The UvA programme provides a fixed 90-EC economics-and-business foundation, a formal Economics major, 30 EC of genuine free-choice space and a final 30-EC major-and-thesis bundle. UCR can build coherent economics/business/data, public-economics/institutions and finance/quantitative pathways, but it does not reproduce the same specialist sequence or a dedicated Economics and Business Economics thesis.
